result.title: From Cross-Section to Cross-Omics: Conditional Cell Nucleus Image Editing in Spatial Transcriptomics
result.summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) platforms simultaneously measure gene expression and capture cell nucleus images at single-cell resolution. A fundamental property of tissue preparation introduces a confounding relationship between the two measurement modalities: sectioning a three-dimensional tissue into a thin slice produces a two-dimensional cross-section whose area depends on the cutting angle. Larger cross-sections expose more cytoplasm, yielding higher mRNA counts, while pathomics features such as nuclear area are measured directly from the same 2D boundary. This sectioning geometry creates an apparent correlation between gene expression and pathomics that reflects the measurement process rather than independent biology. Existing gene-to-image methods generate cell images from gene features but do not support condition-driven editing of existing images across both omics layers. We apply the Manifold-Aware Diffusion (MAD) framework to this dual-omics editing setting, enabling targeted modification of one feature group while preserving the other. Evaluated on podocyte cells from CosMx SMI kidney tissue, MAD achieves MAE=0.6636 and FID=25.19 for pathomics editing, outperforming all compared baselines. A controlled simulation study further confirms that the VAE component in MAD better preserves cross-group independence than CCDM (MAD without VAE).

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对空间转录组数据中切片几何导致的基因表达与病理组学特征混淆，将 Manifold-Aware Diffusion 用于细胞核图像的条件编辑，在保持另一组特征不变的前提下修改目标特征组，并以肾脏足细胞数据评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 属生物医学图像条件生成与编辑应用，虽涉及 VAE 保持跨组独立性的解耦线索，但不涉及视觉推理中的内部状态、证据获取、动态计算或答案生成，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的具体联系。
